liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Garcia plays a long, powerful solo with a pause and a second burst, then a thumping Lesh intro leads into Fire; Reviewer considers the Scarlet/Fire pairing among the finest he has heard [23][29]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Weir plays wild slide guitar on this first-set number [19]
- **Fire on the Mountain** (1 review): Follows Scarlet through a strong transition, with Lesh's thumping bass intro, in a classic-period version [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-07-31.mtx.chappell.sb11.30625.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 182 min; rated 4.79/5 by 14 [1]
- **gd1982-07-31.sbd.jeffm.13310.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 181 min [4]. Said about its sound: Garcia's guitar is low in the mix during Alabama Getaway, then improves and stays fine [4]
- **gd1982-07-31.167996.senn421.beyer.blend.michael.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac1644**: audience recording; 23 songs; 183 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd82-07-31.sbd.martinson.3419.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 181 min; rated 4.18/5 by 33 [9]. Said about its sound: Garcia's guitar sits a bit low in the mix during the first set; Reviewer calls it one of the year's best soundboards, with very good stereo imaging and separation, sounding official; Reviewer's older tape ran slightly fast; this crisp recording at correct speed sounds better [19][22][24][26]

## Around the show

- Show fell on Garcia's 40th birthday, in Texas [24]
- Reviewer's old second-set tape came with a story about paratroopers during the show and a paranoid friend [29]
- Reviewer's 1982 story describes a gravel parking lot outside Austin and a friend who had attended Red Rocks two nights earlier [25]
- Post-drums portion fell after midnight, so people reminded Garcia of his birthday during Morning Dew's quiet section; venue was a racetrack [1]
- Special mail-order tickets for the Austin show at Manor Downs looked sparkling to Mark [35]
- Uploader ranks it in the top five of 1982, alongside 9-17, 4-6, 8-10 and 8-3 [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-07-31.mtx.chappell.sb11.30625.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Chris Chappell; source: SBD: (shn ID 3415); AUD: (shn ID 19017) [1]
- **gd1982-07-31.sbd.jeffm.13310.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff M and Chris Perkins; source: Soundboard>Master Cassette>Cassette>Dat>CDR>EAC>SHN [4]. Also: Tracks were split and renumbered; a 0.56-second dropout in One More Saturday Night was turned into a splice [4]
- **gd1982-07-31.167996.senn421.beyer.blend.michael.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Rodney Michael; transferred by Tim McKenzie;Charlie Miller;Scott Clugston; source: Rodney Michael's Master FOB Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics + Unknown Beyer mic blend > Unknown mixer > Sony D5M > DAT (x0) > Tim McKenzie's CDR's [6]. Also: Jim Vita's Beyer M88 recording supplies patches in Alabama Getaway, Eyes, Drums, Uncle John's Band, Truckin' and Morning Dew [6]
- **gd82-07-31.sbd.martinson.3419.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff M.; source: Soundboard [9]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Michael Priest NM: [23 | November | 2017 | Original Concert Posters](https://original-concert-posters.com/2017/11/23/) [37]
- Poster by Michael: [Grateful Dead Manor Downs Original Concert Poster 1982 Art by Michael Priest NM+](https://pleasantdeadposter.com/grateful-dead-manor-downs-original-concert-poster-1982-art-by-michael-priest-nm.htm) [38]
- Poster by Worthpoint: [GRATEFUL DEAD Poster 1982 Manor Downs Armadillo Artist | #68945629](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/grateful-dead-poster-1982-manor-downs-68945629) [39]
- Poster by @evevintageshop: [Grateful Dead Manor Downs 1982 Poster Shirt](https://evevintage.com/product/grateful-dead-manor-downs-1982-poster-shirt/) [40]
- Photo by Caine Schneider (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 7/31/82 Manor Downs, Austin, TX](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27295846231/) [41]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27295846231/) [42]

citations.author: Caine Schneider
citations.title: Grateful Dead - 7/31/82 Manor Downs, Austin, TX

claims.text: Weir plays wild slide guitar on this first-set number
Garcia's guitar sits a bit low in the mix during the first set
Reviewer calls it one of the year's best soundboards, with very good stereo imaging and separation, sounding official
Garcia plays a long, powerful solo with a pause and a second burst, then a thumping Lesh intro leads into Fire
Follows Scarlet through a strong transition, with Lesh's thumping bass intro, in a classic-period version
Show fell on Garcia's 40th birthday, in Texas
Reviewer's older tape ran slightly fast; this crisp recording at correct speed sounds better
Reviewer finds this copy distorted in places, with big dropouts, and wants a better source
Reviewer's old second-set tape came with a story about paratroopers during the show and a paranoid friend
Reviewer considers the Scarlet/Fire pairing among the finest he has heard
Reviewer's 1982 story describes a gravel parking lot outside Austin and a friend who had attended Red Rocks two nights earlier
Uploader ranks it in the top five of 1982, alongside 9-17, 4-6, 8-10 and 8-3
Post-drums portion fell after midnight, so people reminded Garcia of his birthday during Morning Dew's quiet section; venue was a racetrack
Garcia's guitar is low in the mix during Alabama Getaway, then improves and stays fine
Tracks were split and renumbered; a 0.56-second dropout in One More Saturday Night was turned into a splice
Master cassette by Rodney Michael was transferred to DAT, then Tim McKenzie made the CDR; Charlie Miller coordinated
Jim Vita's Beyer M88 recording supplies patches in Alabama Getaway, Eyes, Drums, Uncle John's Band, Truckin' and Morning Dew
Special mail-order tickets for the Austin show at Manor Downs looked sparkling to Mark
